question: What is cgroup v2, and how does minibox talk to it without any library or systemd?
answer_hinglish:
cgroup (control group) Linux kernel ka feature hai jo processes ke ek group par resource limits lagata hai aur unka usage count karta hai: kitni memory, kitne processes, kitna CPU time. Namespaces process ko 'kya dikhta hai' woh badalte hain, cgroups 'kitna use kar sakta hai' woh. Container = namespaces + root filesystem + cgroup limits.

cgroup v2 ek single unified hierarchy hai jo /sys/fs/cgroup par mounted filesystem ke roop mein dikhti hai. Har directory ek cgroup hai, aur us directory ki files kernel ka interface hain: memory.max mein number likho toh limit lag gayi, cgroup.procs mein pid likho toh woh process us cgroup mein chala gaya, memory.events padho toh counters mil gaye. Koi special syscall nahi, sirf open/read/write/mkdir/rmdir.

minibox bilkul yahi karta hai. minibox/cgroups.py mein do chhote helpers hain, _read aur _write, jo plain open() use karte hain. Cgroup.create mkdir karta hai aur Limits.writes() ke (file, value) pairs likhta hai, Cgroup.add_pid cgroup.procs mein pid likhta hai, Cgroup.stats counters padhta hai, Cgroup.remove rmdir karta hai. PLAN.md ka decision: 'cgroup v2 through files, one leaf per container, no systemd, no libcgroup'. Isi wajah se unit tests (tests/unit/test_cgroups.py) ek plain temp directory ko fake /sys/fs/cgroup bana kar Windows par bhi chal jaate hain: woh check karte hain ki KAUN si files mein KYA likha gaya.
why_needed: Bina limits ke ek container poori machine ki memory, CPU ya process table kha sakta hai. cgroups woh mechanism hai jisse docker --memory/--cpus/--pids enforce karta hai.
real_world_analogy: Ek building ke flats ke bijli meter: har flat (cgroup) ka apna meter aur fuse hai. Fuse ka rating likh do (memory.max), meter padh lo (memory.events). Building ka main board /sys/fs/cgroup hai.
how_it_works: mkdir /sys/fs/cgroup/minibox/<name> -> kernel khud interface files bana deta hai -> limit files mein value likhi -> pid cgroup.procs mein likha -> us process ke saare children automatically usi cgroup mein -> exit par counters padhe -> rmdir.
in_this_project: minibox/cgroups.py poora cgroup layer hai (about 200 lines). CGROUP_ROOT = '/sys/fs/cgroup', PARENT = 'minibox'. container.py::run Cgroup(name) banata hai, cgroup.create(cfg.limits) call karta hai aur cleanup() mein kill, stats, remove.
advantages: Koi dependency nahi, sirf file IO
Har step visible aur debug karna aasaan (cat se padh lo)
Unit tests fake directory par chal jaate hain
disadvantages: systemd se coordinate nahi hota; systemd-managed host par parallel tree banta hai
Error messages sirf OSError/errno ke roop mein milte hain
common_mistakes: cgroup v1 aur v2 ko mix karna (v1 mein har controller ki alag hierarchy thi)
Sochna ki cgroup koi process isolation (dikhna) deta hai; woh sirf resources limit karta hai
Interface files ko normal files samajhna

Child process automatically parent ka cgroup kyun inherit karta hai?
systemd ke saath production mein cgroups kaise delegate karte hain?

question: When you pass --memory 64M to minibox, exactly which files get which values, and how is '64M' parsed?
answer_hinglish:
--memory 64M do kadam se guzarta hai. Pehle cli.py::_size use cgroups.py::parse_size ko deta hai. parse_size ek regex se number aur unit nikalta hai; units binary hain (K = 1024, M = 1 << 20), docker ke --memory jaise. Toh 64M = 64 * 1048576 = 67108864 bytes. '64MiB', '64MB', '64m' sab same result dete hain (unit tests test_parse_size mein), aur '0', '-1M', '1.3' (fractional byte) reject hote hain.

Phir Limits(memory=67108864).writes() pure function hai jo exact list return karta hai: pehle ('memory.max', '67108864'), phir ('memory.swap.max', '0'). Swap wali line jaan-boojh kar hai: server par 4 GB swap hai, aur bina iske kernel container ko OOM-kill karne ki jagah swap kar deta (mutation M15). Cgroup.create in pairs ko leaf /sys/fs/cgroup/minibox/<name>/ mein likhta hai.

Proof do level par: unit test test_limits_writes_order_and_values exact list check karta hai, aur integration test test_limits_are_written_and_read_back container chala kar stats file mein kernel se WAPAS padhi values dekhta hai: {'memory.max': '67108864', 'memory.swap.max': '0', ...}. Matlab kernel ne value accept ki, sirf humne likhi nahi.
why_needed: User friendly '64M' aur kernel ke raw bytes ke beech conversion galat hua toh limit 1000x chhoti ya badi ho sakti hai; isliye parsing alag, pure aur tested hai.
real_world_analogy: Dukaan par '1 kg' bolna aur taraazu par grams mein tolna: conversion fixed rule se hota hai, aur bill (read back) par actual number dikhta hai.
how_it_works: '64M' -> _SIZE_RE match -> 64 * _UNITS['m'] -> 67108864 -> Limits.writes() -> [memory.max, memory.swap.max=0] -> _write(leaf/memory.max) -> kernel validate karta hai -> stats() read back.
in_this_project: cli.py::_size ValueError ko argparse error bana deta hai, toh galat size par container start hi nahi hota. Limits ek frozen dataclass hai, writes() sirf data banata hai, file IO Cgroup.create karta hai.
advantages: Pure function, OS ke bina test
docker jaisi binary units, surprise nahi
Galat input start se pehle reject
disadvantages: 'MB' ko bhi binary maana jaata hai (1 MB = 1 MiB), jo SI units se alag hai
common_mistakes: 64M ko 64000000 samajhna
Sirf memory.max likhna aur swap bhool jaana
Value likhne ke baad read back na karna
follow_up_questions: memory.swap.max = 0 na likhne par kya hota (M15)?

question: What does --cpus 0.5 mean in cgroup v2 terms, and what string does minibox write for it?
answer_hinglish:
cgroup v2 ka CPU limit cpu.max file hai, jisme do numbers hote hain: 'QUOTA PERIOD', dono microseconds mein. Matlab: har PERIOD microseconds mein yeh cgroup zyada se zyada QUOTA microseconds CPU time use kar sakta hai. Quota khatam hua toh cgroup ke threads period ke end tak 'throttled' (ruk jaate hain).

minibox mein cgroups.py::format_cpu_max yeh conversion karta hai: CPU_PERIOD_US = 100_000 (kernel default, 100 ms), quota = round(cpus * period). Toh 0.5 -> '50000 100000' (har 100 ms mein 50 ms), 0.25 -> '25000 100000', 2.5 -> '250000 100000' (multiple CPUs par 250 ms per 100 ms, sirf tab possible jab threads kai CPUs par chalein). --cpus na diya ho toh limit nahi likhi jaati aur kernel ka default 'max 100000' rehta hai, jo test_no_flags_means_no_limits stats file se check karta hai.

Measured (portfolio-a2): 0.5 par busy loop ka share 0.501, 0.25 par 0.252. Dhyan do, yeh 'ek CPU ka half' hai, 'ek core reserve' nahi: cpu.max ek upper cap hai, guarantee nahi.
why_needed: CPU limit ke bina ek busy container baaki sab ka CPU kha leta hai. cpu.max hard cap deta hai jo docker --cpus ka base hai.
real_world_analogy: Mobile data plan jo har ghante 500 MB deta hai: ghante ke beech mein khatam hua toh agle ghante tak ruko. Quota = 500 MB, period = 1 ghanta.
how_it_works: Kernel ka CFS bandwidth controller har period mein cgroup ka runtime count karta hai -> quota cross hua -> threads throttle -> naye period par quota refill.
in_this_project: cli.py::_cpus validate karta hai (> 0, <= 1024, aur quota >= 1 ms). Limits.writes() ('cpu.max', format_cpu_max(cpus)) add karta hai. parse_cpu_max ulta kaam karta hai aur 'max' ko None banata hai.
advantages: Measured numbers quota se match karte hain
disadvantages: Cap hai, guarantee nahi
Bursty workload period ke andar throttle hoke latency spike dekh sakta hai
common_mistakes: 0.5 ko 'half core reserved' samajhna
Period aur quota ki unit milliseconds maan lena (microseconds hain)
cpu.weight (relative share) aur cpu.max (hard cap) confuse karna

question: A container run with --memory 64M exits with code 137. What happened, and how does minibox show it?
answer_hinglish:
137 = 128 + 9, aur signal 9 SIGKILL hai. Shell convention (aur docker) yeh hai ki process signal N se mara toh exit code 128+N. Memory limit ke case mein SIGKILL kernel ke OOM killer ne bheja: cgroup ki memory memory.max (64 MiB) tak pahunchi, reclaim se jagah nahi bani, swap bhi band (memory.swap.max = 0), toh kernel ne cgroup ke andar ek process choose karke maar diya.

minibox mein mapping container.py::exit_code_from_status karta hai: os.waitstatus_to_exitcode signal par negative number deta hai (-9), aur function 128 - (-9) = 137 return karta hai. INIT CMD ka yeh code apne exit code ke roop mein deta hai, host process wahi return karta hai.

Proof test_memory_hog_is_oom_killed mein: shell string ko 27 baar double karke 128 MiB tak le jaata hai, aur assert karta hai returncode == 137, 'survived' print nahi hua, memory.events oom_kill >= 1, memory.peak <= 64 MiB. Bench mein 3 of 3 hogs 137 ke saath mare, peak exactly 64.0 MiB. Debug karte waqt sirf 137 dekh kar OOM mat maano: koi bhi SIGKILL 137 deta hai; confirmation memory.events ke oom_kill counter (stats file) se karo.
why_needed: Production mein 137 sabse common 'container mysteriously died' code hai; isko OOM se jodna aur verify karna aana chahiye.
real_world_analogy: Hotel ka room jisme sirf 2 bags allowed hain: teesra bag laaye toh security (OOM killer) aapko bahar nikaal deti hai, aur register mein 'over limit' ki entry (oom_kill) hoti hai.
how_it_works: Allocation -> memory.max hit (memory.events max++) -> reclaim fail -> OOM killer cgroup ke andar victim chunta hai (oom++, oom_kill++) -> SIGKILL -> waitpid status -> 128+9.
in_this_project: Mapping exit_code_from_status mein; counters Cgroup.stats() se --stats-file JSON mein. README ki L2 table: 137, oom_kill 1, memory.events max 37, peak 64.0 MiB; 16 MiB wala case exit 0, peak 33.5 MiB.
code_example:
# real, minibox/container.py
def exit_code_from_status(status: int) -> int:
    """os.waitpid status -> shell-style exit code (128+N for death by signal N)."""
    code = os.waitstatus_to_exitcode(status)
    return 128 - code if code < 0 else code
advantages: Docker jaisa convention, tools aur logs samajh lete hain
Stats file se cause confirm ho sakta hai
disadvantages: 137 akela cause nahi batata (manual kill -9 bhi 137)
common_mistakes: Har 137 ko OOM maan lena
memory.events padhe bina limit badha dena
Swap on host par yeh expect karna ki limit par turant kill hoga

question: What is a fork bomb, and how does --pids 32 protect the host from one in minibox?
answer_hinglish:
Fork bomb ek program hai jo khud ki copies banata rehta hai, har copy aur copies banati hai, exponential growth. Bina limit ke process table bhar jaati hai aur host par naya process (ssh login bhi) start nahi hota. minibox ke test aur bench mein real bomb hai: bomb() { bomb & bomb; }; bomb.

pids controller ka pids.max file cgroup mein processes + threads ki gintee par hard limit lagata hai. --pids 32 par Limits.writes() ('pids.max', '32') likhta hai. 33va fork() kernel EAGAIN se refuse kar deta hai aur pids.events ka 'max' counter badhta hai.

Measured: 100 sleepers aur fork bomb dono exactly pids.peak 32 par ruke. busybox sh fork fail hone par 'can't fork' print karke us copy ko chhod deta hai, isliye bomb khud hi about 27-30 ms mein exit code 2 ke saath khatam ho gaya. test_fork_bomb_is_stopped_by_pids_max end mein subprocess.run(['/bin/true']) chala kar check karta hai ki host abhi bhi process start kar sakta hai.

Asli lesson ek incident se: mutation M13 ke run mein bomb apne cgroup ke bahar chal gaya, load average 3172 tak gaya, aur systemd ki per-session task limit ne roka. Tab se fork bomb test kisi mutation ke against nahi chalta.
why_needed: Multi-tenant host par ek buggy ya malicious script poori machine ko unusable na kare, isliye har container ki process count limit chahiye.
real_world_analogy: Ek restaurant table jisme 32 kursiyan hain: aur log aaye toh waiter (kernel) mana kar deta hai, baaki restaurant normal chalta hai.
how_it_works: fork()/clone() -> kernel pids controller cgroup ka count check karta hai -> count >= pids.max -> EAGAIN, pids.events max++ -> program error handle kare (busybox sh: give up).
in_this_project: Limits.writes() mein pids < 1 par ValueError (test_limits_reject_zero_pids), cli.py::_pids bhi >= 1 maangta hai. Counters pids.peak aur pids.events stats file mein.
code_example:
# real, tests/integration/test_limits.py (trimmed)
r = box.run("bomb() { bomb & bomb; }; bomb", "--pids", "32", "--stats-file", str(sf), timeout=30)
s = stats(sf)["counters"]
assert r.returncode != 0 and "can't fork" in r.stderr     # busybox sh gives up when fork fails
assert s["pids.peak"] == 32                               # it reached the limit and no further
assert s["pids.events"]["max"] >= 1                       # forks refused by the kernel
assert subprocess.run(["/bin/true"]).returncode == 0      # the host can still start processes
advantages: Hard wall, kernel enforce karta hai
disadvantages: Threads bhi gine jaate hain, multi-threaded app ko zyada limit chahiye
Bomb apne aap tabhi rukta hai jab program fork failure par give up kare
common_mistakes: Sirf memory limit lagana aur pids bhool jaana
Fork bomb test ko bina limit ke chalana
pids.max ko sirf processes ki limit samajhna (threads bhi count)

question: Treat the cgroup v2 interface files as a data store: what record formats do they use, and how does minibox parse each one?
answer_hinglish:
cgroup filesystem ko ek chhota key-value store ki tarah dekh sakte ho: directory = record (ek cgroup), file name = key, file content = value. Lekin value ke teen alag 'schemas' hain aur har ek ka alag parser chahiye.

1) Single value: memory.max, pids.max, memory.swap.max. Content ya number hai ya literal 'max' (no limit). parse_limit 'max' ko None aur baaki ko int banata hai. memory.peak aur pids.peak bhi single int hain.
2) Multi-field single line: cpu.max = 'QUOTA PERIOD', jisme quota 'max' ho sakta hai. parse_cpu_max do parts expect karta hai aur ('50000 100000') -> (50000, 100000), 'max 100000' -> (None, 100000); ek hi part ho toh ValueError.
3) Flat keyed: memory.events, pids.events, cpu.stat, cgroup.events. Har line 'key value'. parse_flat_keyed line ko pehle space par partition karta hai aur dict[str, int] banata hai; value na ho ('novalue') toh ValueError, khaali line skip.

Design ka faayda: parser ko keys pehle se pata hone ki zaroorat nahi. Server ke kernel 7.0 ne memory.events mein sock_throttled aur cpu.stat mein core_sched.force_idle_usec jaise keys diye jo unit tests ke fixtures mein nahi the, phir bhi sab raw JSON mein aa gaye. Yeh schema-on-read hai: kernel naye keys add kare toh code nahi tootta. Tests: test_parse_flat_keyed_memory_events, test_parse_flat_keyed_cpu_stat, test_parse_cpu_max_round_trip.
why_needed: Stats aur limits padhne ke liye sahi parser chahiye; galat parsing (jaise 'max' ko int banana) se crash ya galat numbers aate hain.
real_world_analogy: Ek register jisme kuch pages par sirf ek number hai, kuch par 'naam: number' ki list, aur ek page par 'quota/period' ka do-column entry: har page ka padhne ka tareeka alag.
how_it_works: read file -> format pehchaano (single / two-field / flat keyed) -> parse -> 'max' ko None -> dict ya int.
in_this_project: Cgroup.stats() limits ko raw string (strip karke) rakhta hai aur counters ko parse_flat_keyed / int se parse karta hai. Cgroup.populated() bhi cgroup.events ko parse_flat_keyed se padhta hai.
advantages: Schema-on-read: naye kernel keys automatically aate hain
Har format ka chhota pure parser, unit tested
disadvantages: Nested keyed files (jaise memory.stat ke kuch formats ya io.stat) ke liye yeh parser kaafi nahi
Values int maani gayi hain; float ya text value par ValueError
common_mistakes: 'max' ko int() karna
cpu.max ko single number samajhna
Key list hardcode karke naye kernel keys drop kar dena

question: Describe the layout of the --stats-file JSON that minibox writes. Why are limits strings and counters integers?
answer_hinglish:
Stats file ek JSON document hai jo container.py::cleanup likhta hai, jab cgroup empty ho chuka ho aur rmdir se pehle. Top level keys: 'cgroup' (leaf ka path), 'limits', 'counters', 'exit_code', 'wall_s'. json.dump(..., indent=1, sort_keys=True) se likha jaata hai, toh har run ka diff stable rehta hai.

'limits' mein memory.max, memory.swap.max, pids.max, cpu.max ka content RAW string ke roop mein (strip karke): '67108864', '0', 'max', '50000 100000'. String isliye ki yeh kernel ka exact jawab hai, 'max' aur do-field cpu.max ko bina interpretation ke rakhna hai, aur test seedha dict compare kar sake: test_limits_are_written_and_read_back expect karta hai {'memory.max': '67108864', 'memory.swap.max': '0', 'pids.max': '32', 'cpu.max': '50000 100000'}.

'counters' mein numbers jinpar maths hota hai: memory.events, pids.events, cpu.stat nested dicts (parse_flat_keyed se), aur memory.peak, pids.peak plain ints. bench/limits.py inhi par median, share = usage_usec / (wall_s * 1e6), peak / 1048576 nikalta hai.

Missing file par stats() FileNotFoundError skip karta hai, toh purane kernel par jahan memory.peak nahi hai, key bas absent hogi, crash nahi. Ek real record (l2-memory.json): memory.events max 37, oom_kill 1, memory.peak 67108864, limits.memory.max '67108864', exit_code 137, wall_s 0.201.
why_needed: Bench aur tests ko ek stable, machine-readable record chahiye jo cgroup ke delete hone ke baad bhi bache; cgroup files rmdir ke saath gayab ho jaati hain.
real_world_analogy: Hospital discharge summary: upar 'prescribed limits' (doctor ne jo likha, as-is), neeche 'readings' (numbers jinka graph banta hai), aur end mein outcome.
how_it_works: cgroup.kill + wait empty -> stats(): limits loop (read().strip()), counters loop (parse_flat_keyed), peaks (int) -> update(exit_code, wall_s) -> json.dump sort_keys -> rmdir.
in_this_project: Schema code mein: Cgroup.stats() + cleanup(). Consumers: test_limits.py ka stats() helper aur bench/limits.py ka render(). Raw files bench/reference-results/a2-2026-11-21/*.json mein har run ka poora stats object rakhti hain.
advantages: Ek file mein limits + counters + outcome
disadvantages: Ek hi snapshot, time series nahi (peak ke alawa beech ka shape nahi dikhta)
Limits string hain, consumer ko khud parse karna padta hai
common_mistakes: cgroup delete karne ke baad stats padhne ki koshish
Limits ko int bana kar 'max' kho dena
Stats ko process chalte hue padhna aur final counters miss karna

question: Why does minibox create /sys/fs/cgroup/minibox/<name>/ instead of putting the container directly into /sys/fs/cgroup/minibox/?
answer_hinglish:
Yeh cgroup v2 ke 'no internal processes' rule ki wajah se hai. Rule: ek non-root cgroup jo apne children ko controllers deta hai (cgroup.subtree_control mein +memory etc.), uske andar khud processes nahi ho sakte. Processes sirf leaves mein, aur domain controllers ki limits bhi leaves par. Root cgroup is rule se exempt hai.

Isliye minibox do level banata hai. /sys/fs/cgroup/minibox/ parent hai: uske cgroup.subtree_control mein '+cpu +memory +pids' likha jaata hai taaki children ke paas memory.max, pids.max, cpu.max files aayen. Parent mein koi process nahi. /sys/fs/cgroup/minibox/<name>/ har container ka leaf hai: limits wahan likhe jaate hain aur INIT ka pid uske cgroup.procs mein.

Code mein Cgroup.create: pehle os.makedirs(parent, exist_ok=True) (parent shared hai), phir subtree_control write, phir os.mkdir(self.path) bina exist_ok ke, comment: 'fails if it exists: two containers must never share a cgroup'. Name bhi validate hota hai: [A-Za-z0-9_.-]{1,64}, '.' aur '..' nahi, taaki path traversal na ho (test_cgroup_name_rejected). Default name 'mb-' + 8 hex chars (new_name).

Leaf per container ka faayda: har container ke counters alag (test_two_containers_get_separate_cgroups mein two-a ka pids.max 10, two-b ka 20), aur cleanup ek rmdir.
why_needed: Bina leaf ke ya to limits lag hi nahi sakti (rule) ya do containers ek hi budget share karenge.
real_world_analogy: Ek company ka department (parent) budget categories decide karta hai, lekin kharch sirf teams (leaves) karti hain; department khud koi kharch nahi karta.
how_it_works: mkdir parent -> write '+cpu +memory +pids' to parent/cgroup.subtree_control -> mkdir leaf (kernel leaf mein memory.max etc. bana deta hai) -> limits -> cgroup.procs.
in_this_project: cgroups.py ki module docstring yeh layout aur rule explain karti hai. test_create_writes_limits_into_a_leaf_on_a_fake_root parent ka subtree_control '+cpu +memory +pids' aur leaf ki files check karta hai. test_container_runs_in_its_own_cgroup container ke andar /proc/self/cgroup = '0::/minibox/cg-path-N' dekhta hai.
disadvantages: Shared parent ka removal race (do containers parallel)
Cgroup namespace nahi, toh container apna full path dekhta hai
common_mistakes: Processes ko parent mein daal kar subtree_control likhne ki koshish (EBUSY)
mkdir ko exist_ok=True de dena aur do containers ko ek cgroup mein daal dena
Name validate na karna

question: minibox refuses to run if the root cgroup does not already delegate cpu, memory and pids. Why not just enable them?
answer_hinglish:
Cgroup.create sabse pehle /sys/fs/cgroup/cgroup.subtree_control padhta hai. Agar cpu, memory, pids mein se koi missing hai, toh RuntimeError: 'controllers [...] are not enabled in /sys/fs/cgroup/cgroup.subtree_control'. Comment: 'Enabling them at the root would change the whole host; refuse instead.'

Kyun? Root cgroup ka subtree_control poore host ka setting hai. Usme controller enable karna har top-level cgroup (system.slice, user.slice, docker ke cgroups) ke liye accounting aur interface badalta hai, aur systemd is tree ka owner hai. Ek learning tool ka kaam nahi ki host ka global state chupke se badle, khaaskar portfolio-a2 jaise server par jahan Caddy aur Docker bhi chal rahe hain. Fail-fast better: user ko clear error milta hai aur woh decide kare.

Practically yeh check pass hota hai: SERVER_RUN.md ke read-only checks mein root ke subtree_control mein 'cpuset cpu io memory hugetlb pids rdma misc dmem' pehle se the, 'so minibox never has to change the root cgroup'. Order bhi dhyan do: check makedirs se PEHLE hai, toh refuse karne par kuch nahi banta; unit test test_create_refuses_when_root_lacks_controllers fake root 'cpu io' ke saath RuntimeError (match 'memory') aur 'minibox' directory ka na banna dono check karta hai. Container setup error ke roop mein yeh exit 125 deta hai.
why_needed: Shared production host par tool ko apna scope maintain karna chahiye; global kernel settings badalna doosre services ko affect kar sakta hai.
real_world_analogy: Kirayedar apne flat ki wiring badal sakta hai, building ka main panel nahi; panel mein kuch chahiye toh owner se bolo.
how_it_works: read root subtree_control -> set difference with CONTROLLERS -> missing? raise before any mkdir -> else continue.
in_this_project: Error OSError/RuntimeError/ValueError handler mein pakda jaata hai (container.py::run) aur EXIT_SETUP_FAILED 125 return hota hai; owned['cgroup'] False rehta hai toh cleanup kisi aur ka cgroup nahi chhoota.

# real, minibox/cgroups.py (trimmed)
available = set(_read(os.path.join(self.root, "cgroup.subtree_control")).split())
missing = [c for c in CONTROLLERS if c not in available]
if missing:
    # Enabling them at the root would change the whole host; refuse instead.
    raise RuntimeError(f"controllers {missing} are not enabled in {self.root}/cgroup.subtree_control")
advantages: Clear error, koi half-created directory nahi
disadvantages: Kuch hosts par manual setup chahiye
Systemd delegation (Delegate=yes) use nahi kiya

question: Why does Limits.writes() always write memory.swap.max = 0 together with memory.max, and how was the need proven?
answer_hinglish:
cgroup v2 mein memory.max sirf RAM (page cache + anon) ki limit hai. Swap ki alag limit memory.swap.max hai, jiska default 'max' hai. Matlab sirf memory.max = 64M likhne par cgroup 64 MiB RAM use karega aur baaki anonymous memory swap mein chali jaayegi; OOM kill tab tak nahi hoga jab tak swap bhi na bhare.

portfolio-a2 par 4 GB swap file hai. Toh '--memory 64M' ka matlab 64 MiB nahi, 64 MiB + 4 GB tak ho jaata. Isliye writes() mein comment: 'Without this the kernel swaps the container out instead of OOM-killing it at the limit (portfolio-a2 has a 4 GB swap file), so --memory 64M would not mean 64M of RAM+swap.' Docker ka --memory bhi by default swap ko limit karta hai.

Proof teen jagah: (1) unit test test_memory_limit_always_disables_swap ensure karta hai ki memory diya toh ('memory.swap.max', '0') list mein hai. (2) Mutation M15 (swap line hata di) ne 2 limit tests red kiye: hog swap karke bach gaya, 137 nahi aaya. (3) Read back: stats limits mein memory.swap.max '0'.

Trade-off: swap 0 se limit predictable aur fast fail hoti hai, lekin workload jo thoda swap tolerate kar sakta tha, woh ab seedha OOM-kill hoga. memory.high (soft limit) bhi nahi likha gaya, README ki NOT-done list mein hai.
why_needed: Limit ka matlab user ke expectation se match karna chahiye; host ke swap config par depend nahi.
real_world_analogy: Ek wallet limit jo sirf cash count karta hai, credit card nahi: '500 rupaye limit' bekaar hai jab tak card bhi band na ho.
how_it_works: memory.max hit -> kernel reclaim try karta hai -> anon pages swap out ho sakte hain agar swap.max allow kare -> swap.max = 0 -> reclaim fail -> OOM kill.
in_this_project: Limits.writes() memory ke saath hamesha dono pairs append karta hai; Cgroup.create order mein likhta hai.

# real, minibox/cgroups.py (trimmed)
if self.memory is not None:
    w.append(("memory.max", str(self.memory)))
    # Without this the kernel swaps the container out instead of OOM-killing it at the limit
    # (portfolio-a2 has a 4 GB swap file), so "--memory 64M" would not mean 64M of RAM+swap.
    w.append(("memory.swap.max", "0"))

question: minibox rejects --cpus 0.005. What is the 1 ms rule, and where is it enforced?
answer_hinglish:
Kernel cpu.max mein quota ki ek minimum value accept karta hai: 1000 microseconds (1 ms). Isse chhota quota likhne par write fail hota hai. minibox mein yeh constant CPU_QUOTA_MIN_US = 1_000 hai, comment: 'the kernel rejects a quota below 1 ms'.

Period 100 ms (CPU_PERIOD_US) hai, toh minimum cpus = 1000 / 100000 = 0.01. --cpus 0.005 ka quota round(0.005 * 100000) = 500 us hota, jo kernel minimum se kam hai.

Enforcement do layers par: (1) cli.py::_cpus argparse level par: float parse, 0 < v <= 1024, aur round(v * 100_000) < 1_000 par error 'cpus must be >= 0.01 (the kernel's minimum quota is 1 ms per 100 ms)'. User ko container start hone se pehle saaf message milta hai. (2) cgroups.py::format_cpu_max library level par: cpus <= 0 aur quota < 1000 par ValueError. test_format_cpu_max_rejects_tiny_and_negative 0.005, 0, -1 teeno check karta hai, aur test_format_cpu_max (0.01, '1000 100000') boundary accept karta hai.

Kyun dono jagah? CLI ek caller hai; Limits ko koi aur code (tests, bench, future API) seedha bana sakta hai. Agar sirf kernel par chhodte, toh error mkdir ke baad, limits likhte waqt OSError ke roop mein aata (create() phir remove() karta), aur message cryptic 'Invalid argument' hota.
why_needed: Kernel ke constraints ko pehle validate karne se error jaldi aur samajhne laayak milta hai.
real_world_analogy: ATM jo 100 se kam nahi deta: machine (kernel) mana karegi, lekin app (CLI) pehle hi bata de toh time bachta hai.
how_it_works: --cpus text -> _cpus float -> range check -> quota check -> Limits(cpus) -> writes() -> format_cpu_max (dobara check) -> cpu.max write.
in_this_project: round() use hota hai, toh 0.25 -> 25000 exactly, aur floating point jaisi 0.29999 wali problem quota mein nahi aati. parse_cpu_max(format_cpu_max(0.25)) == (25000, 100000) round-trip test hai.
disadvantages: Limit do jagah likhi hai (CLI mein 100_000 aur 1_000 literal), drift ho sakta hai
common_mistakes: Quota aur period ki unit galat lena
Validation sirf kernel par chhodna
Bahut chhota period chunna (scheduling overhead)

question: Why does minibox read the limits BACK from the kernel instead of trusting what it wrote, and how do the tests use that?
answer_hinglish:
Write karna aur kernel ka effectively apply karna alag cheezein hain. Kernel value ko round, reject ya interpret kar sakta hai, aur ek bug (ya mutation) value likhna hi skip kar sakta hai. Isliye Cgroup.stats() exit par memory.max, memory.swap.max, pids.max, cpu.max kernel se padhta hai aur stats file ke 'limits' mein rakhta hai.

Do integration tests ispar khade hain. test_limits_are_written_and_read_back --memory 64M --pids 32 --cpus 0.5 ke saath 'true' chalata hai aur exact dict compare karta hai: {'memory.max': '67108864', 'memory.swap.max': '0', 'pids.max': '32', 'cpu.max': '50000 100000'}. test_no_flags_means_no_limits bina flags ke check karta hai ki sab kernel defaults hain: 'max', 'max', 'max', 'max 100000' -- matlab minibox ne koi hidden default limit nahi lagayi.

Debugging mein yeh pattern kaam aata hai: agar container expected limit par nahi ruka, pehla sawaal 'kernel ke paas kya value thi?' Stats file is sawaal ka jawab container ke delete hone ke baad bhi deta hai. Bench mein bhi L3 table ka cpu.max column raw stats ke limits se aata hai (rs[0]['stats']['limits']['cpu.max']), typed nahi.

Mutations M14-M17 (memory.max, swap, pids.max, cpu.max na likhna) har ek ne 2-3 limit tests red kiye; read-back test unme se ek common catcher hai.
why_needed: Behavior test (OOM hua ya nahi) ke saath ek direct state check chahiye jo batata hai ki galti 'likha nahi' thi ya 'likha par kaam nahi kiya'.
real_world_analogy: Bank transfer ke baad statement check karna, sirf 'sent' button dabane par bharosa nahi.
how_it_works: cleanup -> kill -> stats(): read(memory.max...).strip() -> JSON -> test compare.
in_this_project: Limits strings mein rakhe gaye hain taaki exact kernel output compare ho. Missing file (controller unavailable) silently skip, aur test dict mismatch par fail karega.

# real, tests/integration/test_limits.py
def test_limits_are_written_and_read_back(box, tmp_path):
    sf = tmp_path / "s.json"
    r = box.run("true", "--memory", "64M", "--pids", "32", "--cpus", "0.5", "--stats-file", str(sf))
    assert r.returncode == 0, r.stderr
    lim = stats(sf)["limits"]
    assert lim == {"memory.max": "67108864", "memory.swap.max": "0", "pids.max": "32", "cpu.max": "50000 100000"}

question: minibox measured 18 ms 'inner' and 105 ms 'outer' to start and stop an empty container. What is in each number?
answer_hinglish:
L0 benchmark 'true' command ko 20 baar chalata hai. Do clocks hain:

Inner (median 18 ms, 17-28): minibox ka apna clock. container.py::run mein started = time.monotonic() cgroup aur overlay dirs banne se pehle set hota hai, aur cleanup() mein wall_s = monotonic() - started stats file mein likha jaata hai. Isme: overlay dirs mkdir, mount plan, cgroup create + limits, unshare(PID), fork INIT, cgroup.procs write, pipe, INIT ke unshare (mount, UTS, IPC, net), hostname, lo up, mounts (overlay, proc, /dev tmpfs, devpts, shm), pivot_root, fork CMD, exec, exit, waitpid, cgroup.kill check, stats read. Note: stats file likhne aur rmdir/rmtree ka thoda hissa wall_s ke baad hai.

Outer (median 105 ms, 101-114): bench/limits.py::run_box subprocess.run ke around time.monotonic(). Isme poora 'python3 -m minibox run' process hai: Python interpreter start, imports, argparse, phir inner kaam, phir cleanup. Toh roughly 85 ms Python startup aur process overhead hai, container ka asli cost about 18 ms.

Interview takeaway: container start 'VM boot' nahi hai; kernel ke liye yeh kuch syscalls hain. Is project mein bottleneck interpreter hai. Daemon model (docker/containerd jaisa long-running process) outer cost hata deta, lekin minibox mein daemon nahi hai. Conditions: 2 vCPU arm64, kernel 7.0, load 0.18.
why_needed: Startup latency batati hai ki containers kitne cheap hain aur cost kahan jaata hai; galat attribution se galat optimization hota hai.
real_world_analogy: Car ka 0-100 time vs ghar se nikal kar highway tak ka time: engine fast hai, lekin parking se nikalna (Python startup) zyada time leta hai.
how_it_works: outer = interpreter start + imports + inner + post-wall_s cleanup; inner = setup syscalls + exec + exit + kill/stats.
in_this_project: bench/limits.py render() L0 table mein med(outer_wall_s * 1000) aur med(stats.wall_s * 1000) likhta hai; raw l0-start.json mein 20 records.

wall = time.monotonic() - t0
...

question: Read the cpu.stat numbers from the L3 table: what do nr_periods, nr_throttled and throttled_usec tell you at --cpus 0.5 and 0.25?
answer_hinglish:
cpu.stat flat keyed file hai. Relevant keys: usage_usec (total CPU time), nr_periods (kitne enforcement periods mein cgroup runnable tha), nr_throttled (kitne periods mein quota khatam hua aur throttle hua), throttled_usec (total kitna time throttled raha).

L3 mein ek busy loop 5 s chala (timeout 5 sh -c 'while :; do :; done'):
- 0.5 (cpu.max 50000 100000): nr_periods 50, nr_throttled 50, throttled 2493 ms, share 0.501. 5 s / 100 ms = 50 periods, aur HAR period mein loop ne 50 ms ke baad quota khatam kiya aur baaki 50 ms ruka. 50 * 50 ms = 2.5 s throttled, measured 2.49 s.
- 0.25: nr_periods 51, nr_throttled 50, throttled 3750 ms, share 0.252. Har period mein 75 ms ruka: 50 * 75 = 3.75 s.
- 1.0: nr_periods 50 lekin nr_throttled 0: limit set hai (periods count ho rahe hain) par ek loop ek CPU se zyada use hi nahi kar sakta, toh 100 ms quota kabhi khatam nahi hota.
- No limit ('max 100000'): nr_periods 0, kyunki bandwidth control active hi nahi.

Debug rule: nr_throttled / nr_periods ratio high hai toh workload quota se CPU-bound hai; throttled_usec batata hai kitni latency add hui. Production mein ek request ke beech throttle aaye toh woh 50-75 ms extra wait karegi, chahe average CPU kam dikhe. Share formula usage_usec / (wall_s * 1e6) hai; wall_s mein startup bhi hai.
why_needed: CPU throttling 'CPU usage normal par latency kharab' ka common hidden cause hai; cpu.stat padhna aana chahiye.
real_world_analogy: Traffic signal jahan har 100 second mein sirf 50 second green: car (thread) ready hai par 50 second khadi rehti hai; nr_throttled = kitni baar red mila, throttled_usec = kitna total wait.
how_it_works: Har period start par quota refill -> thread chalta hai -> runtime >= quota -> throttle, nr_throttled++ -> period end par unthrottle; throttled_usec mein wait add.
in_this_project: Counters Cgroup.stats() se aate hain; bench/limits.py render() median nikalta hai. Tests: test_cpu_hog_is_throttled_by_cpu_max (nr_throttled > 0, 0.35 < share < 0.6) aur test_cpu_hog_without_limit_is_not_throttled (nr_throttled == 0, share > 0.8).

# real, bench/limits.py render (trimmed)
st = [r["stats"]["counters"]["cpu.stat"] for r in rs]
... med([s['usage_usec'] / (r['stats']['wall_s'] * 1e6) for s, r in zip(st, rs)], '{:.3f}') ...
... med([s['nr_periods'] for s in st]) ... med([s['nr_throttled'] for s in st]) ...
... med([s['throttled_usec'] / 1000 for s in st]) ...

disadvantages: Sirf single-threaded loop measure hua
Per-request latency impact measure nahi kiya

question: The first fork-bomb test passed for the wrong reason. What was wrong, and why does the real bomb end by itself in about 30 ms?
answer_hinglish:
SERVER_RUN.md incident 2: pehla test 'bomb() { bomb | bomb & }' use karta tha. busybox sh mein yeh 4 processes se aage badha hi nahi, toh test 'pids.max ne roka' prove nahi kar raha tha, bomb khud hi weak tha. Green test jo limit tak pahunchta hi nahi, kuch prove nahi karta.

Fix do tarah se hua. (1) Bomb badla: 'bomb() { bomb & bomb; }; bomb' -- har call ek background copy aur ek foreground recursion karta hai, real exponential growth. Ab test assert karta hai pids.peak == 32: limit tak PAHUNCHA, aur aage nahi gaya. (2) Ek bounded test add hua: test_spawning_past_pids_max_fails 100 background sleeps chalata hai aur check karta hai 'all-started' print NAHI hua, 'can't fork' stderr mein hai, peak 32.

Bomb apne aap kyun rukta hai? Jab pids.max hit hota hai, fork() EAGAIN deta hai. busybox sh fork fail par 'can't fork' print karke us copy ko error ke saath khatam kar deta hai (retry nahi karta). Copies marti gayin, naye fork bhi fail, aur INIT ka CMD exit code 2 ke saath khatam -> INIT exit -> namespace ki baaki processes SIGKILL. Measured 27 ms median (26-34), exit 2.

pids.events max (refused forks) 31 median par range 29-64, kyunki yeh is par depend karta hai ki us pal kitni copies fork try kar rahi thin; 'can't fork' messages 30 (28-63) usi ke saath chalte hain. Peak hamesha 32.
why_needed: Test ko 'sahi wajah se pass' hona chahiye; yeh check karna ki failure mode actually trigger hua, test design ka core skill hai.
real_world_analogy: Fire alarm test jahan dhuaan hi alarm tak nahi pahuncha: alarm nahi baja toh iska matlab yeh nahi ki alarm kaam karta hai.
how_it_works: bomb & bomb -> copies double -> 32 par fork EAGAIN -> sh 'can't fork' + exit -> CMD exit 2 -> INIT exit -> kernel kills namespace.
in_this_project: Dono tests test_limits.py mein; bench ke BOMB aur SPAWN constants same commands hain. L1 table: 100 sleepers peak 32, events max 1, exit 2; bomb peak 32, events max 31 (29-64), exit 2.

SPAWN = "i=0; while [ $i -lt 100 ]; do sleep 5 & i=$((i+1)); done; echo all-started"
BOMB = "bomb() { bomb & bomb; }; bomb"

Bounded test alag se safe proof deta hai
disadvantages: Bomb ka self-termination busybox sh ke behavior par depend karta hai, bash/dusre programs alag ho sakte hain

Bomb ki growth verify na karna
Unbounded bomb ko bina limit ke chalana

question: Explain the race between forking INIT and moving it into the cgroup, and how the pipe in container.py::run closes it (mutation M13).
answer_hinglish:
Problem: cgroup membership fork par inherit hoti hai, lekin cgroup.procs mein pid likhna fork ke BAAD hi ho sakta hai (pid tabhi pata chalta hai). Host process unshare(CLONE_NEWPID) ke baad INIT ko fork karta hai, phir cgroup.add_pid(init_pid) likhta hai. Agar INIT turant chal pade, toh woh mount setup karke CMD fork kar sakta hai us write se pehle. Tab CMD (aur uske saare children) host ke cgroup mein reh jaate hain -- unlimited. Aur cgroup.procs mein pid likhne se sirf WOH process move hota hai, uske pehle se bane children nahi.

Fix: os.pipe(). Fork se pehle pipe banta hai. INIT (child) write end band karta hai aur os.read(ready_r, 1) par block karta hai. Host read end band karta hai, cgroup.add_pid(init_pid) karta hai, PHIR os.write(ready_w, b'x'). Read sirf tab return hota hai jab host ne cgroup join kar diya. Toh INIT ka koi bhi child cgroup ke andar hi paida hota hai. Comment: 'before INIT can fork: every child is limited too'. Agar add_pid fail ho, except branch INIT ko SIGKILL karke reap karta hai, kyunki woh abhi bhi pipe par wait kar raha hai.

M13 (pipe dono side se hataya) result: 4, 2, 2 failed in 3 runs, aur pehle (jab test 10 containers nahi chalata tha) 4 mein se 1 run poora green. Iske run ke dauran unbounded fork bomb bhi chala aur race haar gaya: bomb SSH session ke cgroup mein chala, load average 3172, systemd ki per-session limit ne roka. Yahi race ka real cost hai.
why_needed: Container ka koi bhi process ek pal ke liye bhi unlimited chala toh limit ka guarantee toot jaata hai; fork bomb jaise case mein woh ek pal kaafi hai.
real_world_analogy: Naye employee ko badge (cgroup) milne se pehle building mein ghusne nahi dete: gate par khada rehta hai (pipe read) jab tak security badge activate karke 'ok' na bole.
how_it_works: pipe() -> unshare(NEWPID) -> fork -> [INIT: close w, read r blocks] [host: close r, write cgroup.procs, write w] -> INIT unblocks -> unshare/mount/fork CMD (CMD inherits cgroup).
in_this_project: container.py::run mein ready_r/ready_w; INIT branch os.read(ready_r, 1). test_container_runs_in_its_own_cgroup 10 containers chala ke har ek mein /proc/self/cgroup == '0::/minibox/cg-path-i' check karta hai, kyunki CMD ka cgroup hi race ka symptom hai.
code_example:
# real, minibox/container.py run (trimmed)
ready_r, ready_w = os.pipe()
os.unshare(os.CLONE_NEWPID)
init_pid = os.fork()
if init_pid == 0:                           # ---- INIT, PID 1 in the new namespace
    os.close(ready_w)
    os.read(ready_r, 1)                     # wait until the host put us into the cgroup
    os.close(ready_r)
    ...
os.close(ready_r)
cgroup.add_pid(init_pid)                    # before INIT can fork: every child is limited too
os.write(ready_w, b"x")
os.close(ready_w)
advantages: Failure path mein INIT ko kill karke clean
disadvantages: Ek extra round trip (bahut chhota)
Host process crash ho jaaye pipe likhne se pehle toh INIT EOF par read return karke bina cgroup ke chal sakta hai (read ka result check nahi hota)
common_mistakes: Sochna ki cgroup.procs likhne se pehle ke children bhi move ho jaate hain
Race ko ek green run se 'fixed' maan lena
Sleep se synchronize karna
follow_up_questions: clone3 ka CLONE_INTO_CGROUP is race ko kaise hatata hai?
os.read ka return value check karna chahiye kya (EOF case)?
Race ko test mein reliably kaise reproduce karoge?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Pipe ek extra fd pair aur ek blocking read hai, lekin yeh fork-then-configure pattern ko safe banata hai. Alternative clone3 + CLONE_INTO_CGROUP (child seedha target cgroup mein paida hota hai) atomic hai, lekin Python stdlib mein clone3 nahi hai aur ctypes se clone Python ke runtime ke saath risky hai.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Host ka add_pid fail (cgroup gayab, EBUSY): except branch INIT ko SIGKILL + waitpid karta hai, exit 125. Host process pipe write se pehle mar jaaye: write end close hota hai, INIT ka read EOF (b'') return karta hai aur code check nahi karta, toh INIT bina limit ke aage badh sakta hai -- yeh ek known gap hai jo README mein alag se nahi likha, code se dikhta hai.
advanced.alternatives: (1) clone3 CLONE_INTO_CGROUP. (2) Host khud pehle cgroup join kare phir fork kare (lekin tab host bhi limited). (3) runc jaisa approach: ek intermediate process jo apna pid khud likhe aur parent sync pipe par confirm kare.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Containers 10x-100x hone par yeh per-container cost same rehta hai (ek pipe). Race window load ke saath BADHTI hai, isliye busy host par pipe aur zaroori hai; M13 ke liye test ko 10 containers tak badhana padha tabhi race reliably dikha.
advanced.production_improvements: os.read ka result check karo (b'x' na mile toh exit). clone3 use karo jahan available. Mutation runs mein dangerous tests deselect karo (ab kiya gaya hai) aur ek host-level safety net (systemd TasksMax) rakho, jaisa incident mein kaam aaya.

question: M13 was a race: before the test was changed, one of four mutation runs was fully green. How do you design a test that reliably catches a race like this?
answer_hinglish:
Race wala bug har run mein nahi dikhta. M13 (pipe hataya) ke saath INIT kabhi-kabhi host ke add_pid se pehle CMD fork kar deta tha, kabhi nahi. Pehle test_container_runs_in_its_own_cgroup ek hi container chalata tha, aur 4 mein se 1 run poora green aaya. Matlab test 75 percent chance se pakadta tha -- mutation 'caught' bolna galat hota agar woh ek green run hi dekha hota.

Fix ke teen hisse: (1) Symptom ko directly observe karo: container ke andar 'cat /proc/self/cgroup' chalao. Race haari toh CMD ka cgroup '/minibox/<name>' nahi hoga. Indirect symptom (jaise limit hit hui ya nahi) zyada noisy hota. (2) Repeat karo: test ab 10 containers chalata hai, har ek alag naam (cg-path-0..9) ke saath, aur har run ka assert message mein run number. Agar ek run mein race ki probability p hai, toh 10 mein kam se kam ek baar pakadne ki probability 1 - (1-p)^10 hai. (3) Comment mein reason: 'Repeated, because the bug this guards against (the command forked before INIT joined the cgroup) is a race.'

Result: M13 ke teen runs mein 4, 2, 2 tests failed (limits + isolation, 45 tests). README is honestly likhta hai 'M13 is a race' -- yeh nahi kehta ki ab 100 percent deterministic hai.

General lesson: race ka test probability badhata hai, certainty nahi deta. Fix ka proof code reasoning (pipe ka happens-before) se aata hai, test ek regression net hai.
why_needed: Flaky detection wala test false confidence deta hai; mutation table ka 'caught' tabhi meaningful hai jab detection reliable ho.
real_world_analogy: Ek kabhi-kabhi aane wali aawaaz car mein: ek test drive mein nahi suni toh problem nahi hai aisa nahi. Dus baar usi road par chalao.
how_it_works: Observable chuno (/proc/self/cgroup) -> N repetitions -> per-run assert message -> mutation ke saath multiple runs -> results honestly report.
in_this_project: test_limits.py ka test_container_runs_in_its_own_cgroup; README mutation table ki M13 row '4, 2, 2 in three runs' aur notes mein '1 of 4 runs fully green' pehle.
code_example:
# real, tests/integration/test_limits.py
def test_container_runs_in_its_own_cgroup(box):
    # no cgroup namespace (see README), so the full host path is visible. Repeated, because the bug

        assert r.stdout.strip() == f"0::/minibox/cg-path-{i}", f"run {i}: {r.stdout!r}"

disadvantages: 10 containers = test slow (har ek about 105 ms outer)
Phir bhi probabilistic

Indirect symptom test karna
