question: Walk through minibox's cgroup cleanup: cgroup.kill, waiting for populated 0, reading stats, rmdir. Why this order, and what can go wrong?
answer_hinglish:
container.py::cleanup tab chalta hai jab host ne INIT ka waitpid kar liya (ya setup fail hua). Order:

1) cgroup.kill(): Cgroup.kill pehle check karta hai directory hai ya nahi, phir populated() (cgroup.events ka 'populated' key flat keyed parse karke). Populated hai toh cgroup.kill file mein '1' likhta hai -- kernel 5.14+ ka feature jo cgroup ke HAR process ko SIGKILL bhejta hai, ek pid list race ke bina (koi naya fork beech mein chhoot nahi sakta). Phir 10 ms ke loop mein populated 0 ka wait, 5 s deadline, warna RuntimeError.
2) Stats: sirf jab --stats-file diya ho. Empty hone ke baad padhna zaroori hai taaki counters final hon (koi process abhi bhi memory/CPU count na kar raha ho).
3) Cgroup.remove(): os.rmdir(leaf). Cgroup directory interface files ke saath bhi rmdir hoti hai, kyunki woh real files nahi; lekin kernel rmdir ko EBUSY deta hai agar cgroup mein abhi bhi process hai -- isliye kill + wait pehle. Phir parent ka rmdir try, EBUSY/ENOTEMPTY/ENOENT ignore (doosra container use kar raha ho).
4) Overlay state dir ka shutil.rmtree; merged agar host namespace mein mounted mila toh RuntimeError.

owned dict ensure karta hai ki naam collision par (doosre container ka cgroup/dir) cleanup kisi aur ka cheez na hataye. Kya galat ho sakta hai: D-state (uninterruptible) process kill ke baad bhi 5 s mein na mare -> RuntimeError, cgroup chhoot jaata. Aur agar minibox khud SIGKILL hua, toh cleanup chalta hi nahi -- README: 'nobody cleans up', koi minibox gc nahi. Tests ka conftest no_leftovers fixture yahi kaam karta hai: bache cgroups mein cgroup.kill likh kar, wait karke, rmdir.
why_needed: Har container ke baad host par koi cgroup, process ya mount na bache; warna resources leak aur next run ke naam collide.
real_world_analogy: Office band karne ka checklist: pehle sab ko bahar nikalo (kill), check karo koi andar nahi (populated 0), meter reading lo (stats), phir taala lagao (rmdir).
how_it_works: isdir? -> populated? -> write cgroup.kill=1 -> poll cgroup.events until populated 0 (deadline) -> stats JSON -> rmdir leaf -> rmdir parent (ignore busy) -> rmtree state.
in_this_project: Cgroup.kill, Cgroup.stats, Cgroup.remove; cleanup() in teeno ko jodta hai. SERVER_RUN incident 3: M6 ke baad bache containers ko server par manually cgroup.kill se roka gaya, phir conftest mein yahi automate hua.
advantages: Atomic group kill, pid-list race nahi
disadvantages: Polling (10 ms) instead of inotify on cgroup.events
minibox crash par koi cleanup nahi
cgroup.kill kernel 5.14+ maangta hai
common_mistakes: Processes rehte hue rmdir karna (EBUSY)
pids list padh kar ek-ek ko kill karna (naye forks chhoot jaate)
Stats ko kill se pehle padhna
follow_up_questions: cgroup.events par poll() / inotify kaise use karoge?
Kernel < 5.14 par cgroup.kill ke bina kaise karoge?
minibox SIGKILL ho jaaye toh recovery kaise design karoge?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Polling simple aur portable hai, cost max kuch ms; inotify/poll on cgroup.events efficient hai par code complex. Kill + wait ek strict ordering deta hai jo rmdir ke EBUSY ko avoid karta hai.
advanced.failure_scenarios: D-state process 5 s mein na mare -> RuntimeError, leaf chhoot jaata. Host process SIGKILL -> kuch nahi chalta, container aur cgroup aur state dir rehte hain (README NOT-done). Stats file write fail (disk full) -> exception, rmdir skip ho sakta hai kyunki remove() usi block mein stats ke baad hai.
advanced.alternatives: Pid list ko freeze (cgroup.freeze) karke ek-ek kill; systemd scope banakar systemd se cleanup karwana; ek supervisor/daemon (containerd-shim jaisa) jo minibox ke marne par bhi cleanup kare.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Bahut saare containers ke saath leaked cgroups jama ho sakte hain jinke naam random hain; ek gc command (bache leaves ke liye kill + rmdir, jaise conftest karta hai) zaroori ho jaata.
advanced.production_improvements: minibox gc/ps add karo, stats write ko try/finally mein rakho taaki rmdir hamesha ho, polling ki jagah inotify, aur shim-style supervisor taaki host process crash par bhi cleanup ho.

question: Mutation M18 (cleanup skips cgroup.kill) was not caught by any test. Why can no test catch it in this design, and why keep the code?
answer_hinglish:
M18 mein cleanup se cgroup.kill hataya gaya (populated 0 ka wait mutation mein bhi tha). Saare limits + isolation tests green rahe: 0 failed. README isko honestly 'not caught, and cannot be with this design' likhta hai.

Reason PID namespace ki semantics mein hai. INIT container ke PID namespace ka PID 1 hai. Jab PID 1 exit karta hai, kernel us namespace ke har process ko SIGKILL karta hai. Container ke cgroup ka har process isi namespace mein hai (INIT cgroup join karke hi fork karta hai, aur saare descendants namespace mein). Host cleanup tab chalta hai jab waitpid(INIT) return ho chuka -- matlab namespace pehle hi khaali ho raha hai. Toh cgroup.kill ke paas maarne ko kuch nahi hota; wait loop thoda intezaar karke populated 0 dekh leta hai. Koi observable farak nahi -> koi test fail nahi.

Toh code kyun rakha? Safety net ke liye: README example deta hai -- future 'exec into a running container' ek aisa process cgroup mein daalega jo INIT ka descendant nahi, toh PID 1 ki maut use nahi maaregi. Tab cgroup.kill hi cgroup ko khaali karega. Ek aur jagah pehle se use hota hai: conftest ka no_leftovers fixture aur SERVER_RUN incident 3 (M6 ke bache containers) mein cgroup.kill se hi roke gaye.

Interview point: mutation 'not caught' hamesha test gap nahi hota; kabhi woh redundant/defensive code dikhata hai. Sahi response hai reason likhna, na ki code delete karna ya fake test banana.
why_needed: Mutation testing ke results ko interpret karna aana chahiye: survived mutant ya to weak test hai, ya equivalent mutant (behavior same). Dono ka response alag hai.
real_world_analogy: Ghar mein smoke detector aur sprinkler dono: agar har baar smoke detector pe hi aag bujh jaaye toh sprinkler kabhi nahi chalega, lekin isse sprinkler bekaar nahi hota.
how_it_works: CMD exit -> INIT returns -> PID 1 exits -> kernel SIGKILLs namespace -> host waitpid returns -> cleanup: populated already 0 ya jaldi 0 -> kill write skipped/no-op -> same result.
in_this_project: cleanup() ka comment: 'normally empty already: PID 1 exiting kills its whole namespace'. Cgroup.kill populated() check karke hi likhta hai.
advantages: Defensive layer future features ke liye
disadvantages: Untested code path: agar kabhi toota toh pata nahi chalega
common_mistakes: Survived mutant dekh kar code delete kar dena
Ek artificial test likhna jo design ke against ho
Report mein 29/29 claim karna
follow_up_questions: Is path ko test karne ke liye kaunsa test hook banaoge (e.g. host se ek extra process cgroup mein daalna)?
Equivalent mutant aur weak test mein farak kaise karoge?
exec feature aane par kaunse tests add karoge?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Code rakhne ka cost chhota (ek file write, populated check) aur future bug ka risk kam; lekin untested code rot ho sakta hai. Alternative hai test-only hook jo ek non-descendant process cgroup mein daale, lekin woh test ko design ke bahar ki state banata.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Agar future mein exec add hua aur cgroup.kill kisi refactor mein toota, toh rmdir EBUSY dega ya cgroup leak hoga -- aur koi existing test nahi pakdega. Agar INIT kabhi PID 1 na rahe (design change), tab bhi.
advanced.alternatives: Ek integration test jo host side se 'sleep' process ko container ke cgroup.procs mein likh de (wo namespace ke bahar hai) aur verify kare ki cleanup ke baad woh mara aur cgroup gaya. Yeh sahi tareeka hai jab exec aaye.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Scale par cgroup.kill ki value badhti hai: zyada containers, zyada chance ki koi bahar ka process (debug tool, exec) cgroup mein ho. 100 containers ke saath leaked process = leaked cgroup.
advanced.production_improvements: Upar wala 'foreign process in cgroup' test add karo, mutation runner mein M18 ko 'equivalent under current design' tag karo, aur exec implement karte waqt yeh test mandatory banao.

question: Deep-dive the OOM measurement: what do exit 137, oom_kill 1, memory.events max 37, memory.peak 64.0 MiB and CONSTRAINT_MEMCG each prove?
answer_hinglish:
L2 benchmark ek busybox shell string ko 27 baar double karta hai (2^27 = 128 MiB string, shell ki copies ke saath isse zyada memory) --memory 64M ke saath. 3 of 3 runs:

- exit 137 (128 + 9): process SIGKILL se mara; 'survived' 0 of 3 mein print hua. Akela yeh OOM prove nahi karta.
- oom_kill 1 (memory.events): kernel ke OOM killer ne is cgroup mein ek process maara. Yeh cause confirm karta hai. 'oom' counter (OOM situation hui) bhi 1 tha raw data mein.
- memory.events max 37: cgroup ne 37 baar memory.max ko hit kiya -- har baar kernel ne reclaim try kiya. Pehle 36 baar reclaim se kaam chal gaya (page cache ya reclaimable memory nikli), 37vi baar nahi, tab OOM.
- memory.peak 64.0 MiB (67108864 exactly): cgroup kabhi limit se upar nahi gaya. Swap 0 tha (memory.swap.max = 0), toh kuch bhi swap mein chupa nahi.
- CONSTRAINT_MEMCG (kernel log): OOM 'memory cgroup' constraint ki wajah se tha, poori machine ka OOM nahi. Host unaffected: baaki services ke processes candidate hi nahi the.

Control case: 16 MiB string (2^24) same 64M limit par exit 0, 3 of 3 survived, oom_kill 0, events max 0, peak 33.5 MiB (33.3-33.5). Yeh dikhata hai limit sirf zyada use par hi bite karti hai. Wall time bhi farak dikhata: hog 197 ms, small 101 ms.

Integration test test_memory_hog_is_oom_killed thoda loose assert karta hai (peak <= 64 << 20, oom_kill >= 1) taaki kernel variance par flaky na ho; exact numbers bench ke raw JSON mein.
why_needed: OOM debugging mein exit code, cgroup counters aur kernel log teeno ko correlate karna aana chahiye; ek signal se galat conclusion nikalta hai.
real_world_analogy: Bank account overdraft: max 37 = 37 baar balance limit tak gaya aur bank ne purane pending payments clear karke jagah banayi; 38vi baar nahi bani toh card block (oom_kill).
how_it_works: alloc -> charge to memcg -> usage >= memory.max -> events max++ -> reclaim -> success? continue : OOM (oom++) -> select victim in memcg -> SIGKILL (oom_kill++) -> peak stays at limit.
in_this_project: Counters Cgroup.stats() se; bench/limits.py HOG_MEM / HOG_MEM_SMALL; render() peak ko / 1048576 karke '{:.1f}' format karta hai.
code_example:
# real, bench/limits.py
HOG_MEM = 'x=a; i=0; while [ $i -lt 27 ]; do x="$x$x"; i=$((i+1)); done; echo survived'
HOG_MEM_SMALL = 'x=a; i=0; while [ $i -lt 24 ]; do x="$x$x"; i=$((i+1)); done; echo survived'
advantages: Host isolation verified via kernel log
disadvantages: Shell string growth ka exact memory profile model nahi kiya
Sirf 3 runs per case
common_mistakes: 137 = OOM maan lena
memory.events max ko OOM count samajhna
Peak ko limit se upar expect karna (swap ke saath dikh sakta tha)
follow_up_questions: memory.high hota toh events mein kya badalta?
OOM victim selection cgroup mein kaise hota hai?
oom_group_kill kya hai aur kab chahiye?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: memory.max hard limit + swap 0 = predictable kill, lekin koi graceful degradation nahi. memory.high throttling aur reclaim pressure deta hai pehle, lekin implement nahi hai (README NOT-done).
advanced.failure_scenarios: Multi-process container mein OOM killer kisi helper process ko maar sakta hai aur main process zinda reh kar broken state mein chale; exit 137 tab nahi aayega. memory.oom.group nahi likha gaya, toh poora group ek saath nahi marta.
advanced.alternatives: memory.high soft limit + userspace OOM handler (systemd-oomd jaisa) jo pressure (PSI) dekh kar pehle action le; ya memory.oom.group=1 taaki container all-or-nothing mare.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Bahut containers ke saath host par memory overcommit ka sawaal: sab limits ka sum RAM se zyada ho sakta hai; har container memcg OOM se bachega lekin global OOM possible. Monitoring ko har cgroup ka memory.events scrape karna padega.
advanced.production_improvements: Stats file ke saath memory.stat ka snapshot, memory.oom.group option, aur ek OOM event ko kernel log se correlate karne ka tool add karo. Sirf exit code par alert mat lagao, oom_kill counter par lagao.

question: With --cpus 1.0 the busy loop used 0.998 of a CPU and was never throttled, same as no limit. Why, and what does that tell you about testing cpu.max?
answer_hinglish:
L3 table: no limit -> share 0.998, nr_periods 0, nr_throttled 0. 1.0 (cpu.max 100000 100000) -> share 0.998, nr_periods 50, nr_throttled 0. 0.5 -> 0.501, 0.25 -> 0.252, dono 50 periods throttled.

Workload 'timeout 5 sh -c while :; do :; done' ek single thread hai. Ek thread ek waqt mein ek hi CPU par chal sakta hai, toh woh 100 ms period mein max 100 ms CPU le sakta hai. Quota 100 ms hai, toh quota kabhi khatam nahi hota -> kabhi throttle nahi. Limit active hai (nr_periods count ho rahe hain, 'max' case mein 0), bas bite nahi karti. README: 'one loop cannot use more than one CPU, so the 1.0 quota is never reached'.

0.998 (1.0 nahi) kyun? Share = usage_usec / (wall_s * 1e6), aur wall_s mein container startup (about 18 ms) aur timeout/sh ka khud ka startup bhi hai jisme loop nahi chal raha. 5.02 s wall mein about 10-20 ms non-loop time.
0.501 aur 0.252 thoda UPAR kyun? README formula kehta hai startup ki wajah se share quota se thoda neeche hona chahiye; measured 0.501 halka sa upar hai. Ek plausible wajah: kernel quota ko time slices mein enforce karta hai aur period ke boundary par thoda overrun ho sakta hai, aur first period throttle se pehle poora chal sakta hai. Yeh project mein alag se measure nahi hua, toh isko hypothesis hi bolna chahiye.

Testing lesson: cpu.max >= threads count ka limit single-thread workload se test nahi hota. Multi-CPU limit (jaise --cpus 1.5) prove karne ke liye multiple busy threads aur utne vCPUs chahiye; portfolio-a2 par 2 vCPU the, aur yeh case measure nahi kiya gaya.
why_needed: Benchmark ka workload limit ko actually stress kare, warna 'limit works' ka claim khaali hai.
real_world_analogy: 100 km/h speed limit wali road par cycle chalana: kabhi challan nahi katega, isse yeh prove nahi hota ki speed camera kaam karta hai.
how_it_works: single thread max = 1 CPU-second per second -> quota 1.0 = 100 ms per 100 ms -> usage < quota hamesha -> nr_throttled 0; quota < 1.0 -> har period quota exhaust -> throttle.
in_this_project: bench/limits.py cpu_hog(seconds) aur loop over (None, '1.0', '0.5', '0.25'). Tests: 0.35 < share < 0.6 at 0.5 (3 s loop), share > 0.8 without limit.
code_example:
# real, bench/limits.py (trimmed)
def cpu_hog(seconds: int) -> str:
    return f"timeout {seconds} sh -c 'while :; do :; done'; true"
...
for cpus in (None, "1.0", "0.5", "0.25"):
    opts = ("--cpus", cpus) if cpus else ()
    cpu.append({"cpus": cpus or "no limit", **run_box(rootfs, state, cpu_hog(cpu_seconds), *opts)})
advantages: 1.0 aur no-limit ek control pair banate hain
disadvantages: Multi-thread / >1 CPU limits untested
Share formula startup include karta hai
common_mistakes: 1.0 par throttling expect karna
Single-thread benchmark se multi-core claim karna
0.501 ko 'limit leak' bolna bina period-level data ke
follow_up_questions: --cpus 1.5 ko 2 vCPU par kaise test karoge?
Share ko sirf loop ke time par kaise compute karoge (startup hata kar)?
Throttling ka tail-latency effect kaise measure karoge?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Single loop simple aur repeatable hai, lekin sirf quota < 1 CPU ko exercise karta hai. Multi-thread workload zyada realistic hota par noise (scheduler, doosre vCPU par load) badhata.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Multi-threaded app jo 2 CPUs use karta hai, --cpus 1.0 par 50 ms mein quota khatam karke 50 ms rukega -- single-thread test yeh kabhi nahi dikhata. Production mein yahi latency spikes ka source hai.
advanced.alternatives: N busy threads (N = vCPUs) ke saath test; period-level sampling (cpu.stat ko har 100 ms padhna); ya cpu.weight based relative sharing test do containers ke beech.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: 10x-100x containers ek host par: total quotas ka sum CPUs se zyada ho sakta hai; tab cpu.max cap hai lekin contention ke time share cpu.weight se decide hota. Benchmark ko contention case bhi chahiye.
advanced.production_improvements: Bench mein multi-thread case aur 'loop-only' share (startup ghata kar) add karo, aur throttling ke effect ko request latency percentile ke roop mein measure karo.

question: A fork bomb ran without its cgroup limit on the shared server during a mutation run. What happened, how was the blast radius contained, and what changed afterwards?
answer_hinglish:
SERVER_RUN.md incident 4 (18:15, mutation M13). M13 cgroup-join wala pipe hatata hai. Pids/memory/cpu mutations ke runs se fork-bomb test pehle hi exclude tha, lekin M13 ke run mein nahi tha. Race haari: CMD INIT ke cgroup join se pehle fork ho gaya, toh bomb SSH session ke apne cgroup mein chala, pids.max 32 ke bina. 1-minute load average 3172 tak gaya.

Kisne roka? Kernel log: 'fork rejected by pids controller in /user.slice/user-1001.slice/session-645.scope'. systemd har login session ko ek scope cgroup mein rakhta hai jiski apni task limit hai -- yeh doosri, host-level safety net thi. Phir bomb ke processes container ke PID namespace ke saath mar gaye (INIT exit -> namespace kill). 18:15:46 par check: 186 processes, memory same, Caddy, Docker, sshd active; 18:24 tak load 0.96.

Kya badla: (1) mutation runner ab fork-bomb test ko HAR mutation ke liye deselect karta hai; README: 'never run against mutated code'. (2) Isliye baaki limit tests bounded hain: 100 sleepers (spawn test), memory hog 2^27 tak -- comments kehte hain 'bounded, so it is also safe to run when the limit is NOT written'. (3) cleanup fixture (no_leftovers) bache cgroups ko kill karta hai.

Lesson: jab aap safety mechanism ko deliberately todte ho (mutation testing), toh woh test jo usi mechanism par depend karke safe hai, dangerous ban jaata hai. Har destructive test ke liye pucho: 'agar code galat ho toh yeh kitna nuksaan karega?'
why_needed: Shared production-like infra par test chalate waqt blast radius design ka part hai; ek test ka bug doosri services gira sakta hai.
real_world_analogy: Car ke brakes test karne ke liye brakes nikalo toh slope wali road par test drive mat karo; flat ground (bounded test) par karo, aur handbrake (systemd limit) on rakho.
how_it_works: mutation removes pipe -> race lost -> CMD in session scope -> bomb grows -> session TasksMax rejects -> load spike -> INIT exits -> namespace killed -> recovery.
in_this_project: Tests: test_spawning_past_pids_max_fails aur test_memory_hog_is_oom_killed ke 'bounded' comments; test_fork_bomb_is_stopped_by_pids_max ka comment 'never run with the limit removed'. README Mutation notes aur SERVER_RUN.md section 3.
code_example:
# real, tests/integration/test_limits.py (comments)
def test_spawning_past_pids_max_fails(box, tmp_path):
    # bounded on purpose (100 sleepers), so it is also safe to run when the limit is NOT written
...
def test_fork_bomb_is_stopped_by_pids_max(box, tmp_path):
    # a real, unbounded fork bomb: every copy starts a background copy and recurses. Without
    # pids.max it would take the whole server down, so it is never run with the limit removed.
advantages: Defense in depth ne kaam kiya (systemd scope)
Incident documented with timeline aur checks
disadvantages: Fork bomb test ab kisi mutation ke against kuch prove nahi karta
Shared server par risk zero nahi hua
common_mistakes: Destructive test ko mutation suite mein bina soche shaamil karna
Sirf ek layer (apna cgroup) par bharosa
Incident ke baad host health check na karna
follow_up_questions: Is test ko safely mutation ke against kaise chala sakte ho (VM, nested cgroup)?
systemd TasksMax kaise configure hota hai?
Postmortem mein kaunse metrics capture karoge?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Bounded tests safe hain par 'real' attack nahi dikhate; unbounded bomb real hai par sirf sahi code ke saath chal sakta hai. Project ne dono rakhe aur unbounded ko mutation se bahar rakha.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Agar systemd ki session limit na hoti (ya root shell bina scope ke), toh bomb process table bhar deta, sshd naye login fork nahi kar paata aur server reboot tak unreachable ho sakta tha.
advanced.alternatives: Mutation runs ko ek disposable VM mein chalana; ya poore test run ko ek parent cgroup (pids.max) ke andar rakhna -- toh mutated code bhi us outer cgroup se bahar nahi ja sakta.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Zyada mutations aur parallel runs ke saath aisa risk multiply hota; har runner ek outer limited cgroup mein ho, aur dangerous tests ke liye allowlist.
advanced.production_improvements: Test runner ko 'sudo systemd-run --scope -p TasksMax=... -p MemoryMax=...' jaise outer limit ke andar chalao, dangerous tests ko marker se tag karke mutation mode mein auto-skip, aur har run se pehle/baad host health snapshot (jaise SERVER_RUN ka before/after diff).

question: Two containers share the parent /sys/fs/cgroup/minibox. How is that handled, and what race is still left (ENOENT, exit 125)?
answer_hinglish:
Har container apna leaf banata hai, lekin parent 'minibox' shared hai. Create: os.makedirs(parent, exist_ok=True) -- doosra container pehle se bana parent reuse karta hai -- phir subtree_control write, phir os.mkdir(leaf). Remove: leaf rmdir, phir parent rmdir try; agar EBUSY / ENOTEMPTY (doosra leaf abhi hai) ya ENOENT (kisi aur ne pehle hata diya) toh ignore. Matlab 'jo aakhri jaaye, light band kare'.

test_two_containers_get_separate_cgroups: two-a (--pids 10) aur two-b (--pids 20) parallel chalte hain, dono 'ready' print karke stdin par ruk jaate hain. Test leaves ke pids.max alag (10, 20) check karta hai, phir sirf a ko khatam karta hai aur assert karta hai ki two-b abhi bhi hai aur two-a gaya: parent doosre ke liye bacha. Unit test test_remove_keeps_parent_used_by_another_container fake root par same logic.

Bacha race (README NOT-done list): container A apna leaf hata kar parent rmdir kar raha hai, aur usi pal container B create mein hai. Sequence: B ka makedirs dekhta hai parent hai (exist_ok) -> A parent rmdir kar deta hai (khaali tha) -> B ka subtree_control write ya mkdir(leaf) ENOENT. Woh OSError run() ke except mein pakda jaata hai aur exit 125. Data corrupt nahi hota, sirf B fail hota hai.

Kyun fix nahi kiya? Window chhota hai aur result safe failure hai. Fix ke options: parent ko kabhi delete na karna (sabse simple), ENOENT par create ko retry karna, ya ek lock file (flock) create/remove ke around.
why_needed: Shared resources ka lifecycle (kaun banata, kaun hatata) concurrency ka classic problem hai, file system level par bhi.
real_world_analogy: Shared office ka aakhri employee light band karta hai: agar usi pal koi naya employee darwaza khol raha tha, woh andhere mein atak jaata hai (ENOENT) aur wapas jaata hai (125).
how_it_works: A: rmdir leaf -> rmdir parent succeeds. B (interleaved): makedirs ok (saw parent) -> write parent/subtree_control -> ENOENT -> except -> 125.
in_this_project: Cgroup.remove errno filter; container.py run ka except (OSError, RuntimeError, ValueError) -> EXIT_SETUP_FAILED. owned['cgroup'] False rehta hai toh B kisi aur ka cleanup nahi karta.
advantages: rmdir ki atomicity (khaali ho tabhi hatega) natural reference counting deta hai
disadvantages: Rare spurious 125
Har create subtree_control dobara likhta hai
common_mistakes: Parent ko delete karne se pehle 'koi leaf hai?' listdir se check karna (TOCTOU)
Errno filter na karna aur doosre container ka cleanup crash karna
follow_up_questions: flock se yeh race kaise band karoge?
Parent hamesha rehne de toh kya nuksaan?
ENOENT par retry kitni baar safe hai?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: rmdir ko hi 'is it empty' check banana lockless aur simple hai, lekin create path par check-then-act race chhodta hai. Parent ko permanent rakhna race hata deta par host par ek khaali cgroup chhodta (SERVER_RUN ka 'no /sys/fs/cgroup/minibox' cleanup proof phir nahi milta).
advanced.failure_scenarios: Burst mein bahut containers start/stop hote hain toh spurious 125 ki frequency badhegi. Agar koi wrapper 125 ko permanent failure maane toh jobs fail honge.
advanced.alternatives: flock(/run/minibox.lock) create aur remove ke around; create mein ENOENT par loop (makedirs dobara); ya systemd delegated slice jo permanently rehta hai.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: 100 parallel containers: rmdir/mkdir contention aur race window dono badhte; lock serialization ka cost milliseconds mein, startup 18 ms ke comparison mein chhota.
advanced.production_improvements: Create mein ENOENT par bounded retry (2-3 baar) sabse sasta fix; lambe term mein parent ko daemon/systemd ke own karne do aur minibox sirf leaves manage kare.

question: Explain the measurement method of bench/limits.py: raw JSON, generated tables, median with min-max, and recorded conditions. Why is it built this way?
answer_hinglish:
bench/limits.py ke do modes hain. Measure mode (Linux + root): conditions.json likhta hai, phir L0 (20 runs 'true'), L1 pids (sleepers + bomb, har ek 3 runs), L2 memory (hog + small, 3 runs), L3 cpu (no limit / 1.0 / 0.5 / 0.25, 3 runs) chalata hai. Har run run_box() se: python3 -m minibox run ... --stats-file temp.json, aur result record mein cmd, opts, exit, outer_wall_s, stderr_lines, stderr_head, stdout_tail aur POORA stats object. Har level ki list ek raw JSON file mein (l0-start.json ... l3-cpu.json).

Render mode (kahin bhi chal sakta hai): raw files padh kar markdown tables banata hai, SUMMARY.md likhta hai, aur --update-readme ke saath README ke <!-- MEASURED:START --> aur <!-- MEASURED:END --> markers ke beech ka hissa replace karta hai, ek 'generated ... do not edit' comment ke saath. Module docstring: 'Every number in the tables comes from a --stats-file ... or from this script's own clock. Nothing is typed by hand.'

med() median aur (min-max) deta hai. Median kyun: 3 runs mein ek outlier mean ko kheench leta; range variance dikhata (bomb ka events max 31 (29-64) -- yeh variance khud ek finding hai). conditions: date, kernel, machine, cpus, cpu_model, python, load average before (0.18), MemAvailable, commit (BENCH_COMMIT env, yahan 13f7698). Bina conditions ke number reproducible nahi.

Design ke faayde: numbers re-derivable (koi bhi raw JSON se tables dobara bana sakta hai), README aur data kabhi drift nahi karte, aur measure ka expensive/risky hissa (server par root) cheap/safe hisse (render, PC par) se alag hai. SERVER_RUN timeline: bench 18:05:16-18:06:22, results copy kiye gaye aur check kiya ki unmein addresses ya host names nahi.
why_needed: Performance claims tabhi credible hain jab raw data, method aur conditions saath hon, aur numbers haath se type na hue hon.
real_world_analogy: Lab report jisme raw readings ki notebook (JSON), calculation ka fixed formula (render), aur experiment ki conditions (temperature, date) sab attached hain; summary table notebook se hi banti hai.
how_it_works: measure: conditions -> run_box x N per case -> raw JSON per level -> render. render: raw -> med(...) -> markdown -> SUMMARY.md -> update_readme between markers.
in_this_project: Raw data bench/reference-results/a2-2026-11-21/ mein committed hai; README ka Measured section usi se generated.
disadvantages: 3 runs statistical confidence ke liye kam hain
Ek hi machine
Runs interleaved nahi (cases order mein), time-based drift case ke saath correlate ho sakta
common_mistakes: Sirf best run report karna
Mean use karna chhote samples par
Conditions (load, kernel, commit) na likhna
Table haath se README mein copy karna
follow_up_questions: Runs ko randomize/interleave kyun karna chahiye?
Confidence interval chahiye toh kitne runs?
Different hardware ke results ek README mein kaise rakhoge?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Raw + generated approach ek extra step (render) aur ek data directory maangta hai, lekin har number traceable banata hai. Median robust hai par 3 samples par range hi asli information hai; percentiles (p99) ke liye kaafi data nahi.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Agar bench background load ke saath chala (load average check sirf start par hai), toh numbers inflate; conditions mein sirf 'before' load hai, 'during' nahi. Stats file na bane (minibox crash) toh run_box json.load par fail aur poora measure ruk jaata.
advanced.alternatives: pytest-benchmark ya hyperfine jaise tools (outer timing ke liye), perf/eBPF per-phase timing ke liye; ya CI mein har commit par bench aur trend graph.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: 10x runs ke saath p95/p99 meaningful hote; 100 parallel containers ka bench (throughput aur cgroup contention) ek naya level (L4) hota jo abhi nahi hai.
advanced.production_improvements: Runs interleave karo, load average after bhi record karo, run_box mein stats-file missing ko record karo (skip nahi), aur per-phase timers (cgroup, mounts, exec) minibox ke stats mein add karo.

question: If minibox were used to run many containers on a production host, what would break in its cgroup handling, and how would you redesign it?
answer_hinglish:
Pehle honestly scope: minibox ek learning runtime hai, security boundary nahi (no user ns, caps, seccomp, cgroup ns). Production ke liye pehle wahi fix karne honge. Sirf cgroup layer dekhein toh kya tootega:

1) Crash recovery nahi: README ke anusaar agar minibox SIGKILL ho toh container chalta rehta hai aur cgroup + state dir bache rehte hain; koi gc/ps/stop nahi. Many containers par leaked random-naam (mb-xxxxxxxx) cgroups jama honge. Tests mein yeh kaam conftest ka no_leftovers karta hai (cgroup.kill + wait + rmdir), production mein ek 'minibox gc' chahiye jo wahi kare -- lekin pehle state (kaun sa leaf kis live process ka hai) record karna padega.
2) Host process hi supervisor hai: har container ke liye ek Python process (about 105 ms start) jo signals forward aur cleanup karta. Docker mein yeh kaam containerd-shim jaisa chhota process karta hai jo daemon restart se bhi bachta hai.
3) systemd ke saath ownership: minibox /sys/fs/cgroup/minibox seedha root ke neeche banata hai. systemd host par sahi tareeka delegated subtree (Delegate=yes wala unit/slice) hai, taaki systemd use apna samjhe.
4) Shared parent race (ENOENT -> 125) burst load par zyada dikhega.
5) Limits limited hain: no io, cpuset, memory.high, oom.group; stats sirf exit par ek snapshot.

Redesign: ek chhota per-container shim process (runtime exit ho jaaye, shim rahe), state file per container (name, init pid, cgroup path), delegated systemd slice as parent (kabhi delete nahi -> race gayab), clone3 CLONE_INTO_CGROUP (M13 race design se gayab), gc command, aur live metrics (memory.events, cpu.stat) periodically scrape karke exporter ko dena. Aur sabse pehle security hardening.
why_needed: Senior interview mein yeh dikhana zaroori hai ki aap prototype aur production ke gap ko specifically, apne code ke reference se, bata sako.
real_world_analogy: Ghar ka khana banana vs restaurant chalana: recipe (cgroup writes) same hai, lekin restaurant ko inventory (state), shift handover (shim), aur closing checklist (gc) chahiye.
how_it_works: Today: runtime process = supervisor, cleanup in finally, parent created/removed per run. Proposed: shim + state file + permanent delegated parent + gc + periodic stats.
in_this_project: README NOT-done list (no gc/ps/stop/exec, SIGKILL leaves cgroup and state, parent race, no IO/cpuset/memory.high), conftest no_leftovers (gc ka prototype), PLAN.md (no systemd, no libcgroup decision).
advantages: Gaps clearly documented, toh roadmap clear
Core mechanisms (leaf, kill, read-back) production patterns se match
disadvantages: Abhi production-ready nahi
Security boundary nahi
common_mistakes: Learning runtime ko production mein daal dena
Sirf cgroup fix karke security ignore karna
Cleanup ko sirf finally block par chhodna
follow_up_questions: Shim process exactly kya karta hai?
systemd delegation mein Delegate=yes kya deta hai?
Live metrics scrape karne ka cost kya hai?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Per-container shim ek extra process aur IPC laata hai lekin runtime crash ko container crash se alag karta hai. systemd delegation host ke saath cooperation deta hai lekin systemd dependency laata hai, jo PLAN.md ne simplicity ke liye avoid kiya tha.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Runtime crash -> orphan containers + leaked cgroups; burst start/stop -> ENOENT 125; host reboot -> state dir /run/minibox (tmpfs) gaya, cgroups bhi gaye, but overlay upper dirs agar persistent disk par hon toh stale.
advanced.alternatives: runc + containerd (industry standard), crun (C mein, fast startup), ya systemd-nspawn / systemd-run --scope jo cgroups systemd se hi manage karwata hai.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: 10x: 105 ms Python start per container aur ek Python supervisor per container memory cost; 100x: cgroup tree operations aur stats scraping ka load, leaked cgroups ka accumulation. Daemon + shim model yahan zaroori.
advanced.production_improvements: State file + gc + ps/stop, shim, delegated parent, clone3, memory.high/oom.group/io limits, periodic metrics, aur sabse pehle user ns + caps drop + seccomp.

question: Design a test and measurement plan that would extend minibox's limit proofs to multi-CPU limits and many containers in parallel. What do the current results NOT prove?
answer_hinglish:
Current results kya prove karte hain: ek single busy loop par cpu.max < 1 CPU exact hai (0.501, 0.252); pids.max ek hard wall hai (peak 32); memory.max + swap 0 OOM kill deta hai (peak 64.0 MiB, CONSTRAINT_MEMCG); start cost 18 ms inner. Sab ek 2 vCPU arm64 VM par, 3 runs (L0: 20), ek container ek waqt mein.

Kya NAHI prove karte: (1) cpu.max >= 1 CPU (1.0 par single loop kabhi throttle nahi hua, toh 1.5 ya 2.0 untested). (2) Multiple containers ke beech contention: kya 0.5 + 0.5 do containers mein bhi exact rehta hai jab dono busy hon? (3) Parallel start/stop ka behavior: sirf do containers wala test hai (two-a/two-b), aur parent removal race measured nahi, sirf README mein reasoned. (4) Throttling ka latency effect (sirf totals hain). (5) Doosre kernels/x86.

Plan: L4 multi-CPU: workload mein N busy loops (sh mein N background loops) aur --cpus 0.5, 1.0, 1.5 on 2 vCPUs; expect share = min(N, cpus) aur 1.0 par ab nr_throttled > 0. L5 contention: do containers parallel, dono 1.0, dono N=2; total host CPU 2, share har ek ka about 1.0. L6 parallel lifecycle: 50-100 containers 'true' ko parallel batches mein start/stop, count karo kitne 125 aaye (parent race), aur end par /sys/fs/cgroup/minibox na ho. L7 latency: ek container mein loop jo har 10 ms timestamp likhe, throttling ke gaps ka histogram.

Method same rakho: har run ka --stats-file raw JSON, conditions.json, render se generated tables, median (min-max). Safety: sab bounded (timeout), runner ek outer limited cgroup/scope mein, kyunki fork-bomb incident (load 3172) dikha chuka hai ki galat code ke saath unbounded test shared server ko hila sakta hai. Mutation: M17 (cpu.max nahi likha) ko L4 se bhi check karo.
why_needed: Senior engineer ko yeh pata hona chahiye ki uske benchmarks ka scope kya hai aur next claim ke liye kaunsa experiment chahiye.
real_world_analogy: Ek bridge ko ek truck ke saath test kiya: ek truck ka weight sahi hai, lekin 20 trucks ek saath ya cycle-to-truck mix ka koi data nahi.
how_it_works: Current: 1 container, 1 thread, sequential. Proposed: N threads (L4), M containers concurrent (L5), parallel lifecycle (L6), time-resolved latency (L7); same raw-JSON + render pipeline.
in_this_project: bench/limits.py ka measure() naye levels ke liye extend hoga (run_box reuse), test_limits.py ka test_two_containers_get_separate_cgroups parallel pattern (popen) ka base hai. Yeh levels abhi exist NAHI karte.

Parallel test bina outer limit ke shared server par
Race ko reasoned se 'measured' bolna

cpu.weight test kaise add karoge?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Zyada levels = zyada server time aur risk; har level ko bounded aur outer-limited rakhna padega. Parallel tests flaky ho sakte hain, isliye median + range aur zyada runs.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Parallel bench mein host ki memory/CPU khatam ho kar doosri services affect kar sakti hain; parent race ke 125 results run_box ko tod denge (stats file nahi banegi) agar handle na kiya.
advanced.alternatives: Dedicated test VM (disposable), ya nested cgroup/scope jisme poora bench chale; tools jaise stress-ng workload ke liye (lekin brief stdlib-only hai, toh sh loops better).
advanced.scale_10x_100x: 10x/100x containers par measure karo: start throughput (containers/s), cgroup create/remove latency, aur leaked cgroups = 0 check; ye production readiness ke indicators hain.
advanced.production_improvements: run_box ko missing stats-file tolerate karna sikhao (record as failure), conditions mein 'load during' add karo, aur har naye level ke saath ek matching mutation (jaise M17 for L4) chalao taaki pata chale woh level kuch pakadta hai.
